tool_input.command:
cat >> /Users/rogerlin/Downloads/SwiftMandarin-main/agent-progress.txt <<'EOF'

### 2026-08-22 — iPhone screenshot triage: word lookups failed and poisoned the vocabulary list

- Report: four iPhone screenshots (~/Downloads/swm). Visible defects: (1) Word Details showed "Could not translate word" in red for 服从 and 命令; (2) the Vocabulary list had 指挥/命令/服从 all "defined" by the identical full-sentence translation "Obey orders and obey orders."; (3) the Translate screen's input header read ENGLISH over Chinese text (服从命令听指挥) and the output header read CHINESE over an English-led card, because the toggle said EN→中 while auto-detect translated 中→EN; (4) the Word Details "Chinese" speak button wrapped to "Chi-nese".
- Root causes and fixes:
  1. `WordTranslationService.systemOrAITranslate` (and the batch path) used `TranslationSession(installedSource:target:)` on iOS 26+ with NO fallback — that initializer throws whenever the language pack isn't downloaded, so every per-word lookup on such a device failed even with a working AI provider configured. Both paths now catch the system-session error and route through `AIWordExplanationService.translateWithProvider` when `AIModelSettings.shared.isAnyProviderAvailable`, mirroring the pre-iOS-26 branch (shared `aiTranslate`/`mergeAITranslations` helpers).
  2. `WordDetailPopover`'s catch block assigned the sentence-level `contextTranslation` into `englishDefinition`, and Save fell back to `contextTranslation` too — so every word saved after a failed lookup stored the whole sentence's translation as its definition (the screenshot's identical-definitions rows). The error path now leaves the gloss empty (context is still shown, labeled, in the error text), Save passes only the word-level gloss and is disabled when there is none, and a "Try Again" button re-runs the lookup. Copy-with-Pinyin similarly no longer pastes the sentence in place of a missing gloss. Also fixed latently wrong saves of English headwords, which stored the English word itself as its own definition instead of the Chinese gloss (`wordDefinition` = the side opposite the headword).
  3. `TranslateView` section headers/speak voices used the toggle's `sharedState.direction` even though translation itself auto-detects (`detectedTranslationDirection`). New `displayedDirection` (toggle when empty, detected once text exists) now drives both headers and both Speak buttons — the voice bug meant Mandarin text was narrated with an en-US voice whenever the toggle mismatched.
  4. The popover action row's labels ("中文" → localized "Chinese", EN, Copy, Save) now use the existing `.fitSingleLine()` helper instead of wrapping mid-word.
- Files: `Services/WordTranslationService.swift`, `Views/Components/RubyTextView.swift`, `Views/TranslateView.swift`. No new strings beyond reused catalog keys ("Try Again").
- Tests: generic iOS Simulator Debug and macOS Debug builds via Xcode-beta; iOS clean (only the pre-existing "duplicate build file" warnings), macOS log checked the same way.
- Not done / data note: vocabulary entries already saved with sentence definitions on the device are stored data; the code fix prevents new ones but existing rows need re-saving (delete + tap the word again) or an AI re-analysis pass. The sentence-level translation quality itself ("Obey orders and obey orders." for 服从命令听指挥) is model output, not app logic.
EOF
echo appended
